Use smooth fields on Minkowski coordinate space with $x^0=ct$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Components of $x$ are measured in metres. Fix the Dirac matrices and adjoint of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], so $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$ and $\bar\psi=\psi^\dagger\beta$.

For the SI-normalization bookkeeping, let $c>0$ (m s$^{-1}$), $\hbar>0$ (J s), $\mu_0>0$ (N A$^{-2}$), a real charge parameter $q$ (C), and a mass parameter $m>0$ (kg) be symbolic inputs; put $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. In the current SI, $c$ and $h$ are defining constants while $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined; the formula below keeps $\mu_0$ symbolic and assigns it no numerical value. Use the lower-potential convention
$$A_a=(-\phi/c,\mathbf A),\qquad F_{ab}=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a,$$
where $A_a$ has units T m, $\phi$ is in volts, and $\mathbf A$ is in T m. Define
$$S_0=\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c},\qquad a_a=A_a/S_0,\qquad f_{ab}=\partial_aa_b-\partial_ba_a,$$
$$\mu=mc/\hbar,\qquad g=q\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}=q/\sqrt{\epsilon_0\hbar c},\qquad D_a=\partial_a-ig a_a.$$
Thus $a_a$ and $\mu$ have units m$^{-1}$, $f_{ab}$ has units m$^{-2}$, and $g$ is dimensionless. For $\psi$ with units m$^{-3/2}$, both $-\tfrac14 f_{ab}f^{ab}$ and $\bar\psi(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu)\psi$ have units m$^{-4}$; their integral over $d^4x$ is dimensionless and represents the action divided by $\hbar$ in this normalization.

For a real smooth gauge parameter $\chi$ in webers, put $\alpha=\chi/S_0$ (dimensionless) and use
$$A'_a=A_a+\partial_a\chi,\qquad a'_a=a_a+\partial_a\alpha,\qquad \psi'=e^{ig\alpha}\psi.$$
The induced covariant derivative is $D'_a=\partial_a-ig a'_a$. These are formal mathematical conventions for the later conditional deductions. They do not adopt a measured value of $\mu_0$, identify $q$ with an electron charge, impose charge quantization, or assert that interacting continuum fields exist.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Under the explicit Countable Choice assumption [A2], the canonical momenta from the displayed kinetic term are $p_j=\partial L/\partial\dot z_j=i\hbar\bar z_j/2$ and $\bar p_j=\partial L/\partial\dot{\bar z}_j=-i\hbar z_j/2$. Moving each velocity-independent momentum expression to the left gives exactly $C_j=0$ and $\bar C_j=0$. The finite canonical calculation uses the positive $\hbar$ fixed in [F1].

For each $j,k$, bilinearity and the elementary brackets give
$$\{C_j,C_k\}=0,\qquad\{\bar C_j,\bar C_k\}=0,\qquad \{C_j,\bar C_k\}=\{p_j,(i\hbar/2)z_k\}+\{-(i\hbar/2)\bar z_j,\bar p_k\} =-\frac{i\hbar}{2}\delta_{jk}-\frac{i\hbar}{2}\delta_{jk}=-i\hbar\delta_{jk}.$$
Antisymmetry gives $\{\bar C_j,C_k\}=i\hbar\delta_{jk}$, which is exactly the displayed block matrix $M$.

Multiplication of the two displayed block matrices gives $MM^{-1}=M^{-1}M=I_{2N}$; each off-diagonal product is $(-i\hbar)(i/\hbar)=1$ or $(i\hbar)(-i/\hbar)=1$, and the diagonal blocks are zero. Because $\hbar>0$, $M$ is invertible, so these primary constraints are second class by definition.

The canonical coordinate bracket $\{z_j,\bar z_k\}$ is zero. In the Dirac correction, the only nonzero factors are $\{z_j,C_\ell\}=\delta_{j\ell}$ and $\{\bar C_m,\bar z_k\}=-\delta_{mk}$. Hence
$$\{z_j,\bar z_k\}_D =0-\delta_{j\ell}(M^{-1})_{C_\ell,\bar C_m}(-\delta_{mk}) =(M^{-1})_{C_j,\bar C_k}=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\delta_{jk}.$$
The same formula has no nonzero block for $\{z_j,z_k\}_D$ or $\{\bar z_j,\bar z_k\}_D$, so both vanish.

For a smooth $H(z,\bar z)$, the only nonzero reduced coordinate bracket in $\{z_j,H\}_D$ is with $\bar z_j$, so step 4.1 gives $\dot z_j=\{z_j,H\}_D=-i\hbar^{-1}\partial H/\partial\bar z_j$. Multiplying by $i\hbar$ proves the stated equation. The calculation remains finite-dimensional for every $N$ and introduces no infinite-dimensional Poisson bracket or fermionic anticommutator.
